newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico state stockpiles old wheat in price war.
newsitem.headline: Mexico state stockpiles old wheat in price war.

text.p: Wheat growers in the central Mexican state of Guanajuato have in warehouses around 10,000 tonnes of grain from the 1995-1996 crop cycle because of a price war with millers.
"To date, there are around 10,000 tonnes of wheat in storage from the previous crop because of problems over price," Hector Lugo, a Guanajuato state farm development official, told Reuters.
Lugo said the problem centered on differences over price despite the fact that millers have entered into a gentleman's agreement to buy the grain.

Millers have offered 1,400 pesos per tonne while the growers are asking 1,650 pesos. Lugo expected the growers to sit out the price war and wait for a spike in international prices to exert pressure on millers.
Lugo said he expected the 1996-1997 cycle to produce 25 percent less wheat in Guanajuato state than the previous cycle. He gave no production figure in tonnes.
"We are expecting to see around 90,000 hectares planted in the 1996-1997 cycle, a drop from the 120,000 hectares planted in the previous cycle," he said.
